title: Model Attributes and Constraints
description: Learn how to configure primary keys, unique constraints, compound indexes, defaults, and table mappings using field and block attributes.

data.text: Attributes in Prisma modify models or fields. Prisma differentiates between **field attributes** (prefixed with `@`) that modify a single column, and **block attributes** (prefixed with `@@`) that apply to multiple columns or the entire model.

rows: Defines the primary key of the model
Sets default value (autoincrement, now, uuid, cuid)
Enforces unique values on the column
Maps Prisma field to different database column name
Creates a database index for fast querying
Maps model name to a different physical table name

data.title: Comprehensive Constraints Example
data.content: Demonstrating composite unique constraints, indexes, and custom column mappings.
data.code:
model OrderItem {
  id        String   @id @default(uuid())
  orderId   String   @map("order_id")
  productId String   @map("product_id")
  quantity  Int      @default(1)
  unitPrice Decimal  @map("unit_price") @db.Decimal(10, 2)
  createdAt DateTime @default(now()) @map("created_at")

  order     Order    @relation(fields: [orderId], references: [id], onDelete: Cascade)
  product   Product  @relation(fields: [productId], references: [id])

  // Prevent duplicate items for the same product in a single order
  @@unique([orderId, productId], name: "order_product_unique")

  // Add composite index for order query performance
  @@index([orderId, createdAt])
  @@map("order_items")
}

data.title: Clean TypeScript with `@map` and `@@map`
data.text: In relational databases, snake_case (`order_items`, `created_at`) is the standard naming convention, while JavaScript and TypeScript prefer camelCase (`orderItems`, `createdAt`). Using `@map` and `@@map` lets you write clean TypeScript in code without violating database naming standards.

data.title: Key Takeaways
points: Use `@id` for single primary keys and `@@id` for composite keys.
`@@index` ensures query performance on frequently filtered columns.
`@map` bridges TypeScript camelCase and PostgreSQL snake_case.
